svg.title: Diagram 2. Components (35): thin views, hidden TS brain with bottle-mcp, per-MOG main agents, Rust core and the IPC boundary
svg.desc: Three lanes inside the device: view windows (V1 hub, V2 MOG views, V3 cards), the hidden brain window (T1-T15, bottle-mcp, AgentGuard) and the Rust core (R1-R17, with R16 AgentHost and R17 BottleMcpServer) inside the red dashed secret boundary, with R12 IpcGateway on the boundary. A main agent harness per MOG (Claude Agent SDK or Codex) calls bottle-mcp tools and Genie One MCP. The external column holds the Databricks CLI process, the OS keychain, the workspaces, optional Lakebase (v1) and the browser. The IPC contract lists insert_text for UC1. The Rust loopback adds the token for agent model and Genie One MCP calls (ARC-7). A lower panel shows restart and crash recovery.
svg.text: Diagram 2. Components: views, hidden brain, main agents, Rust core, IPC boundary (35 components: V1-V3, T1-T15, R1-R17)
Device: Bottle (one OS process; one shared agent runtime child)
WebView windows (Tauri 2.12.5+): thin views + hidden brain, no secrets
Hidden brain window (TS): all domain logic
Main agent runtime: 1 process, N sessions (U11)

SessionGuard rows still apply after restart (app crash row of Section 7.2).
Diagram 2. Components. The hidden brain window
owns domain logic; the main agent decides through
bottle-mcp under AgentGuard. The Rust core owns
capture, credentials and every socket. R12 checks
every command. V = view, T = TS brain, R = Rust core.
